project-charter.title: Observe the Motorcycle Suspension

cards.title: Client Brief & Application Context
cards.body: Bajaj Auto Suspension Development Division has assigned you to design and analyze the rear twin-shock helical compression spring for a 150cc commuter motorcycle.

cards.title: Real-World Operating Parameters
cards.body: The rear suspension uses twin spring-damper units to support rider payload and absorb road shocks. Each spring must carry a maximum working load of 1,250 N without exceeding allowable torsional shear limits or experiencing solid coil binding.

cards.title: Engineering Objectives & Scope
items: Observe motorcycle suspension construction and trace the load path.
Label suspension components on Engineering Asset EA-12.
Determine spring geometry (wire diameter d, coil diameter D, free length Lf).
Calculate Wahl factor K, maximum torsional shear stress, spring rate k, and solid height Ls.
Verify Factor of Safety (FoS) and recommend design modifications.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I have read and understood the EA-12 Project Charter for Motorcycle Suspension Spring Design.

component-identification.title: Identify the Suspension Components
component-identification.description: Student engineering asset showing motorcycle rear shock absorber and helical compression spring assembly.

labels.feedback: Coiled mechanical spring storing strain energy and absorbing road shocks.
Hydraulic damper controlling spring rebound oscillations.
Top spring locator transmitting load to frame mounting eye.
Bottom spring seat supported by preload adjustment collar.
Lower bushing connecting suspension unit to rear swingarm.
Upper eyelet connecting suspension unit to motorcycle frame.
Internal damper shaft guiding axial spring compression along spring axis.
Stepped collar adjusting initial spring compression for variable passenger load.

load-path.title: Understand the Load Path
load-path.prompt: Analyze the load path and energy transformation during rear wheel impact over a road bump.

mcq.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the mechanical roles of the helical spring and the hydraulic damper?

options.label: The helical spring compresses under load to store strain energy and provide restoring force; the damper dissipates kinetic energy to damp oscillations.
The damper supports the entire weight of the motorcycle while the spring prevents fluid leakage.
The spring converts road bumps into hydraulic pressure while the damper acts as a rigid lock.
The spring and damper operate independently with zero load interaction during riding.

design-requirements.title: Establish Design Requirements
given: Maximum Working Load per Spring (P) = 1,250 N
Modulus of Rigidity for Spring Steel (G) = 78,500 N/mm²

spring-geometry.title: Determine Spring Geometry
given: End Style: Squared and Ground Ends (Total Coils Nt = N + 2)

components.name: Spring Wire Diameter & Torsional Shear Strength
components.label: Torsional Shear Evaluation

components.name: Active Coil Count & Free Length Clearance
components.label: Deflection & Solid Binding Evaluation

options.title: ACCEPT SPRING DESIGN AS SUITABLE
options.description: Calculated torsional shear stress (373.76 N/mm²) is below allowable material limits (450 N/mm²), providing FoS = 1.20 under maximum bump load.

options.title: REJECT DESIGN / INCREASE WIRE DIAMETER TO 8.5 MM
options.description: For harsh road impacts with two heavy riders, FoS = 1.20 provides narrow fatigue margin. Increasing wire diameter d to 8.5 mm reduces shear stress to 310 N/mm² and boosts FoS to 1.45.

options.title: SPECIFY SHOT PEENING & SQUARED-GROUND ENDS
options.description: Specify shot peening to induce compressive surface residual stress, increasing fatigue strength under cyclic suspension compression, with squared and ground coil ends for flat seating.

options.title: UPGRADE TO CHROME VANADIUM STEEL (50CrV4)
options.description: Upgrade spring material to Chrome Vanadium steel to increase allowable shear stress to 550 N/mm² for heavy-duty or off-road motorcycle variants.
